pairs.difference: A (cap): the board's top edge is a firm contour, but the map also holds a bevel line under the rim, a double-lined cord and separate tassel strands, so inner edges vary in weight. B (hat): one even, unbroken dark line runs round the cone and brim like a sticker cut-line, with almost nothing inside except the buckle's double square. B's outline_darkness (-0.132) is further outside the real range than A's (-0.096).
pairs.fix: Let the hat's silhouette vary: crisp at the buckle and tip, melting softly into shadow under the brim. Add a thin fold crease where the cone meets the band. No even line around the shape.

pairs.difference: A (cauldron): a thin, even contour wraps pot and legs, the rim and handles carry stacked concentric lines, and the cobbles add a busy web of hard cracks. Edges are spread evenly rather than gathered at the focus. B (gloves): the left glove's boundary nearly dissolves, with soft lost edges and sharp crease lines only at the thumb fold. B's background stripes are harder than the hero, though, and both cards sit below the real subject density, so this is a weak call.
pairs.fix: Keep the sharpest edges on the cauldron rim and bubbles. Let the lower belly fade softly into its shadow, and make the cobble joints shallow and faint.

pairs.difference: A (scarf): thin selective contour with soft fold transitions; only the badge has tight concentric rings. B (broom): the bristles are parallel, sausage-like strands, each with a thick dark groove on both sides. The grooves clump into a heavy black mass at the tips, heavier than any inner line in the real lessons. Real internal seams are thin and precise.
pairs.fix: Draw the bristles as thin, tapering fibres with fine gaps between them, and only a few deep grooves near the binding. Fade the tips softly instead of ending every strand in a dark line.

pairs.difference: A (envelope): firm contour with double lines on the stamp and postmark, and a dense tiny-town photo. This is busy but controlled, with the focus sharpest. B (wheel): scratchy grain on the rim and bold black plank lines and cracks in the floor, which compete with the hero. Density and outline numbers are close and in or near the real range. Each card has one suspicious trait, and neither has a decisive edge tell.

A (candelabra): near-black doubled contours follow every turning on the stem, arms, cups and base. Metal reflections read as thick stacked lines, and subject density 0.23 is far above the real maximum of 0.157. B (lamp): thin glass contour, clean rim lines on the brass, and density 0.128 in range.
pairs.fix: Render the brass with broad smooth reflections and only a few thin bright rim edges. Remove the stacked dark bands along the stem and base, and keep the sharpest edges at the candle flames.

pairs.difference: A (drink): thin, precise glass walls, ice cube edges and fine bubbles, with the straw and umbrella crisp at the top. B (crystal ball): the smoke is drawn as dozens of hair-like streak lines where it should be a soft gradient, and the rim carries doubled contours. Soft material ends up with edges that belong on a hard object. Both are below the real subject range, so density does not decide it.
pairs.fix: Paint the smoke inside the ball as a soft, blurry glow with no streaks or line work. Keep one thin, clean rim on the glass and sharpen only the small sparkle stars.

pairs.difference: A (cat): a thick dark band hugs the ears, head, tail and paws like a drawn outline, and outline_darkness (-0.162) is well outside the real range (-0.054 to 0.097). Whiskers and eye rings are heavy graphic lines. B (fountain): many thin stepped rims and soft water edges with no halo band, though the background is noisy at 0.046, the top of the range.
pairs.fix: Remove any dark rim around the cat. Let the fur fade softly into the wall on the shadow side, with a crisp edge only at the ears and eyes. Draw whiskers thin and tapering.

pairs.difference: A (house): every wall, trim, window and muntin has its own doubled contour, and the outer walls wobble with a soft grey band along them. Edge weight is the same from roof to door, with no focus. The moon also has a heavy ring. B (lighthouse): clean straight stone seams, sharp lantern and railing, and clouds that are mostly soft, matching the labelled REAL lighthouse in the lessons.
pairs.fix: Keep the sharpest edges on the door and glowing windows. Make the roof and wall edges simpler and cleaner, draw stone seams as thin, sparse gaps, and leave the moon as a soft disc with no ring line.

pairs.difference: A (coffin): a bevel double-line runs evenly round the lid and base, the wood carries long uniform grain strokes, and the distant trees and gravestones are soft. Background density 0.013 sits just under the real minimum of 0.015. B (chess table): the tile grid and stone are crisp, with thin crack lines and hard foliage strokes in the tree crowns. Background density 0.065 is high but within the real range.
pairs.fix: Cut the even double line around the lid to a single thin seam, and fade the wood grain toward the far end. Give the grass and distant trees small crisp marks so the scene has as much edge detail as the hero.

pairs.difference: A (tombstone): the outer boundary is soft and blurry while the crack is a thick black groove, far heavier than the rest. Pocks are little ringed dots, and subject density 0.069 is below the real minimum of 0.087. B (sneakers): very dense, with heavy panel outlines and mesh, at the top of the real density range, and outline_darkness -0.1 falls outside the real range. Both have faults, so this is a low-confidence call.
pairs.fix: Give the stone a crisp, clean silhouette and carved cross edge, and make the crack a thin, sharp hairline. Drop the ringed speckles and use a few faint chips.

pairs.difference: A (pumpkin): the outer boundary and ribs are faint and blurred, with subject density 0.038 well under the real minimum of 0.087. Only the carved face has a sharp double line, and the table planks are much harder than the hero, so the hierarchy is inverted. B (duck): firm clean silhouette, crisp wing seam and spring coils, with the edges strongest on the hero.
pairs.fix: Sharpen the pumpkin's silhouette and draw thin, clean creases between the ribs. Make the plank gaps soft and shallow so the table stays quieter than the pumpkin.

pairs.difference: A (balloons): thin, soft contours with lost edges where balloons overlap and a crisp knot at the ribbon, close to the restraint of real cards, though subject density 0.028 is low. B (buoy): heavy dark lines down the cone walls and under the foam, and hard ripple rings and cloud contours. Background density 0.021 exceeds the real maximum of 0.017, so the background competes with the hero.
pairs.fix: Soften the clouds and ripples to gentle low-contrast shapes with no hard lines. Thin the dark line down the buoy's sides and keep the sharpest edges on the bell.

pattern: Generated cards give themselves away by edge weight spread too evenly. Doubled dark contours and thick grooves wrap every part, whether metal turnings, trim or bristles, while real cards keep inner seams thin and let boundaries go soft or lost in shadow. Hierarchy also fails: the sharpest edges land on incidental spots such as a tombstone crack, floor planks or smoke streaks, not at the focus. Subject density often falls outside the real range on the high side (p05) or the low side (p10, p11), and soft materials get line work.
